people.name: Mr. Ahmed Elgammal
people.title: Professor of Computer Science and Director of the Art and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Rutgers University, United States of America /Egypt
people.session: Discussion: The IP in the Machine – Untangling IP Issues Behind the Models
bio: Dr. Ahmed Elgammal is a professor at the Department of Computer Science at Rutgers University. He is the founder and director of the Art and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory at Rutgers, which focuses on data science in the domain of digital humanities. He is also an Executive Council Faculty at the Center for Cognitive Science at Rutgers University.

Prof. Elgammal published over 200 peer-reviewed papers, book chapters, and books in the fields of computer vision, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. His research on knowledge discovery in art history and AI art generation, received wide international media attention, including reports on the Washington Post, New York Times, the Guardian, the Daily Telegraph, CBS, NBC News, Science News, New Scientist, and many others. His art has been shown in several technology and art venues in Los Angeles, Frankfurt, San Francisco, and New York City. Dr. Elgammal also led the AI team which completed Beethoven 10th symphony using emerging LLMs, which was a pioneering project in music generation, receiving worldwide media coverage, and several awards.

Dr Elgammal received the National Science Foundation CAREER Award in 2006. Dr. Elgammal received his M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees in computer science from the University of Maryland, College Park, in 2000 and 2002, respectively.

people.name: Ms. Kim Jordahl
people.title: Associate General Patent Counsel, Office of General Counsel, Dana- Farber Cancer Institute, United States of America
people.session: Discussion: The IP in the Machine – Untangling IP Issues Behind the Models
bio: Kim Jordahl is Associate General Patent Counsel at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston, Massachusetts, a world leader in cancer research and treatment.

Kim has more than 30 years of experience in intellectual property law, spanning private practice, corporate legal departments, and academic research institutions. Prior to joining Dana-Farber in 2023, she operated solo practice for more than 15 years, representing Fortune 50 companies and similarly sized privately held global enterprises. Her earlier experience includes in-house positions with Solvay and The Pillsbury Company, as well as positions with both large general practice law firms and specialized intellectual property boutiques. She has served in various leadership roles within the American Intellectual Property Law Association (AIPLA), including as a member of its Board of Directors.

Kim oversees the preparation and prosecution of patent applications in the areas of diagnostics, cellular therapies, methods of treatment, and bioinformatics, and manages related intellectual property portfolios. She advises investigators and institutional stakeholders on intellectual property matters, navigating the intersection of scientific innovation, patent protection, and the dissemination of research findings.

Her broader practice has encompassed patent portfolio development, domestic and international patent prosecution, and intellectual property strategy across a wide range of technologies and industries. Her perspective on artificial intelligence and intellectual property is informed by the practical challenges of protecting emerging technologies, including AI-enabled innovations, while supporting the research, collaboration, and knowledge sharing that are fundamental to scientific advancement.

people.name: Mr. Daheo Lee
people.title: Managing Partner, Lee, PI IP LAW, Republic of Korea
people.session: Discussion: The IP in the Machine – Untangling IP Issues Behind the Models
bio: Daeho Lee is the founding and managing partner of PI IP LAW, a Seoul- based intellectual property law firm. A Korean patent attorney with 18 years of experience, he specializes in patents for artificial intelligence and software, advising AI developers ranging from startups to global technology companies on protection strategies covering model architectures, training data pipelines, and deployment technologies.

His practice spans patent prosecution, litigation, and IP strategy. He has handled Korean court cases concerning data, web crawling, and the protection of software services, and has prosecuted patent applications directed to data structures and AI model structures before the Korean Intellectual Property Office — experience that directly informs the questions this panel addresses.

Mr. Lee has been recognized as one of IAM's Patent 300 Global Leaders since 2024 and as a Trade Mark Star by Managing IP since 2022. Beyond client work, he leads the AI transformation of his own firm, building agent-based automation systems and MCP-based services that connect clients' AI assistants directly to the firm's case management systems — giving him a practitioner's view of "the IP in the machine" from both sides: protecting AI, and practicing with it.

people.name: Ms. Burcu G. Özcan Büyüktanır
people.title: Professor of Civil Law, Head of the Department of Civil Law, Director of the Health Law Research Center, Faculty of Law, Hacettepe University, Türkiye
people.session: Discussion: The IP in the Machine – Untangling IP Issues Behind the Models
bio: Prof. Dr. Burcu G. Özcan Büyüktanır is a Professor of Law at Hacettepe University, Faculty of Law, Ankara, Türkiye, where she serves as Head of the Department of Civil Law and Director of the Health Law Research Center.

Her research focuses on intellectual property law, particularly patent law, pharmaceutical patents, and copyright law. Her academic interests also include liability law, contract law, family law, consumer law, and health law.

Her recent research explores the intersection of artificial intelligence and intellectual property rights, including the patentability of AI-related inventions, copyright protection, and the balance between technological innovation, competition, and the public interest.

She has also been involved in a research project with the Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Culture and Tourism entitled “Artificial Intelligence and Copyright: A Comparative Law and Economics Analysis Across Countries.”

In addition to her academic work, she also practices law, providing legal advice and consultancy in her areas of expertise. She is actively involved in mediation and professional training and serves as an expert witness in copyright and patent law matters.

people.name: Fr. Paolo Benanti, T.O.R.

people.name: Ms. Inbar Preiss
people.title: Senior intellectual property correspondent, MLex, Netherlands
people.session: Horizon Scan: What’s Next for IP and AI?
bio: Inbar Preiss is a Brussels-based senior intellectual property correspondent for MLex, a news publication specializing in regulatory and legal risk. Her reporting spans patents, copyright and trademarks, with a focus on the relationship between IP , artificial intelligence and innovation.

She follows developments across European institutions and courts, examining how legal decisions and policy choices affect businesses, creators and technology developers. Coverage includes copyright disputes over AI training, emerging licensing models and the development of Europe’s Unified Patent Court.

Previously, she covered digital assets policy and regulation for DL News and The Block. She reported on the development and implementation of the EU’s first crypto markets regulation, alongside litigation and criminal proceedings testing the boundaries of responsibility in decentralized technologies. Her coverage of the Tornado Cash prosecution explored questions about software developers’ liability, financial privacy and the legal implications of open-source code.
From crypto to AI, she reports on how frontier technologies test the limits of existing law, and what that means for the people and businesses using them.

Earlier, she worked with Brussels-based publications including The Parliament Magazine and Are We Europe. She holds a bachelor’s degree in international relations from University College Utrecht and a master’s degree in international politics from KU Leuven.

people.name: Ms. Danielle Boyer

people.session: Horizon Scan: What’s Next for IP and AI?

people.name: Mr. Paul Goldstein
people.title: Stella W. and Ira S. Lillick Professor of Law, Emeritus, Stanford University, United States of America
people.session: Horizon Scan: What’s Next for IP and AI?
bio: A globally recognized expert on intellectual property law, Paul Goldstein is the author of an influential five-volume treatise on U.S. copyright law and a one-volume treatise on international copyright law. He has authored twelve books including five novels. Some of his other works include Copyright’s Highway: From Gutenberg to the Celestial Jukebox, a widely acclaimed book on the history and future of copyright and Intellectual Property: The Tough New Realities That Could Make or Break Your Business. Havana Requiem, his third novel, won the 2013 Harper Lee Prize for Legal Fiction.

In 2015 Paul Goldstein was inducted by Intellectual Asset Management into the IP Hall of Fame, which honors those who have helped to establish intellectual property as one of the key business assets of the 21st century. He currently serves as of counsel at Morrison & Foerster in their intellectual property group and has been regularly included in Best Lawyers in America. He has served as chairman of the U.S. Office of Technology Assessment Advisory Panel on Intellectual Property Rights in an Age of Electronics and Information, has been a visiting scholar at the Max Planck Institute for Foreign and International Patent, Copyright, and Competition Law in Munich, Germany and was a founding faculty member of the Munich Intellectual Property Law Center. In addition, before joining the Stanford Law School faculty in 1975, he was a professor of law at the State University of New York at Buffalo Law School.

people.name: Ms. Aishwarya Karnataki
people.title: Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, Glovatrix, India
people.session: Horizon Scan: What’s Next for IP and AI?
bio: Aishwarya Karnataki is the Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Glovatrix, an Indian assistive technology company developing AI- powered tools to make communication more accessible for Deaf people. An electronics and electrical engineering graduate of Manipal University, she combines technical training with an entrepreneurial focus on independence, dignity and inclusion.

At Glovatrix, she leads work on Fifth Sense, a wearable system that uses sensors and artificial intelligence to translate sign language into speech and text. She is also Co-founder of Mira, which develops AI-powered translation of text and speech into Indian Sign Language through a digital avatar. Together, these efforts address communication barriers in both directions, with applications across hospitality, workplaces, education, healthcare and public services.

Her commitment began with an encounter with a Deaf child during her school years and deepened through witnessing the consequences of inaccessible communication in everyday life. She works closely with Deaf colleagues and language experts to ground product development in the needs and experiences of the communities it serves.
Under her leadership, Glovatrix was named a winner of the WIPO Global Awards in 2025. Her work has also been presented at the United Nations AI for Good Summit in Geneva.

Aishwarya brings a founder’s perspective to discussions on AI and intellectual property: how to turn technical innovation into practical tools, build sustainable ventures, and ensure that the benefits of emerging technologies reach people too often excluded from their design.

people.name: Mr. Qoane Mothibeli
people.title: Founder & Managing Director, JuliGerm (Pty) Ltd, Lesotho
people.session: Horizon Scan: What’s Next for IP and AI?
bio: Qoane Mothibeli is a Lesotho-based technology entrepreneur, AI innovator, and Founder and Managing Director of JuliGerm (Pty) Ltd, a technology-driven venture-building and consulting company developing solutions at the intersection of artificial intelligence, geospatial intelligence, and sustainable development.

He leads the development of Orbi, an AI-powered geospatial intelligence platform that combines Earth observation, satellite imagery, geospatial analytics, and conversational AI to make complex land and environmental information accessible to individuals, businesses, and institutions. His work spans precision agriculture, climate intelligence, agricultural insurance, and digital monitoring systems, including geospatial technology initiatives supporting the United Nations World Food Programme's agricultural insurance efforts in Lesotho.

Qoane is a recipient of the United Nations Research Institute for Social Development (UNRISD) Explorer Award, recognizing his contributions to innovative approaches to sustainable development. He is also an Included VC Africa Fellow and has participated in international technology, entrepreneurship, and innovation initiatives.

With an academic background in Philosophy and Sociology from the National University of Lesotho, complemented by training in data science, artificial intelligence, and technology entrepreneurship, he brings an interdisciplinary perspective to emerging technologies.

His interests include AI governance, intellectual property, technological sovereignty, and equitable access to advanced technologies, particularly the opportunities and challenges of building and deploying AI solutions in African markets.

people.name: Mr. Terry Winograd
people.title: Professor Emeritus of Computer Science, Stanford University, United States of America
people.session: Horizon Scan: What’s Next for IP and AI?
bio: Terry Winograd is Professor Emeritus in the Computer Science Department at Stanford University. During his 40 years of teaching and research he created and directed the Human-Computer Interaction Group and the teaching and research program in Human-Computer Interaction Design at Stanford. He was a founding faculty member of the Hasso Plattner Institute of Design (the "d.school").

Winograd did pioneering research in artificial intelligence, in particular natural language understanding, during his PhD program at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Lab in the 1960s. His 1986 book with Fernando Flores, Understanding Computers and Cognition, marked a major departure in the philosophy underlying AI. He was a founding member and National President of Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility. He is a member of the ACM CHI Academy and an ACM Fellow. He received the 2011 CHI Lifetime Research Achievement Award. He is a Fellow of the Stanford Human-Centered AI Institute and has been a consultant to a number of companies, including Google, founded by Stanford students from his projects.
